Definition
Definition
In this lesson, you will observe the operation of typical light transmitters and receivers.
INTRODUCTIONM
In the first part of the experiment, you will measure the voltage and current characteristics of photometric and radiometric light transmitters.
You will use luminescent red, green, amber, & infrared LEDs, and an incandescent lamp..
In the second part of the experiment, you will measure the characteristics of light receivers.
You will use a photocell, photodiode, photovoltaic, and phototransistor.
Finally, you will apply an analog signal to a light transmitter and see the results on the output of a light receiver.

LIGHT RECEIVERSITLE
In this experiment, you will observe the operation and measure the characteristics of typical light receivers.
EXPERIMENT
The light receivers are mounted on the right hand side of the PC130-251 experiment card.
EMITTERS-LIGHT-DETECTORS
SENSITIVITY
The photocell circuit consists of PC1 and a common collector amplifier Q1.
Switch S7 isolates the photocell when in the TEST position.
The photodiode and photovoltaic circuit consist of PD1, PV1, and Q2.
S8 selects which light receiver is connected to the amplifier. It also is used for isolation purposes.
The phototransistor circuit consists of PT1 and Q3.........
S9 isolates the light receiver when in the TEST position. R10 controls sensitivity.
EMITTERS-LIGHT-DETECTORS
SENSITIVITY
The four black housing on the right hold the light receivers. They are also used for the fiberoptic connection.
In this part of the experiment, you will connect different light transmitters to the light receivers using the fiberoptic cable.
The photocell is the top light receiver and the phototransistor is the bottom light receiver.
The fiberoptic cable is made of fibers that reflect light. Light entering one end of the cable is reflected to the other end, light transmission.
The grip is where you place your fingers to insert and remove the cable from the connectors on the PC card.
Always use the grip to prevent damage to the cable when inserting and removing the cable.
The lock is used to snap and hold the probe in the connector.
The probe houses the end of the fiber cable. Look at the end of the probe and you can see the fibers.
